sec1.titulo: What a CEO needs from a news briefing
abertura: In your lesson you tell a CEO what a news article really says.
Mark the **three** things a CEO usually needs from that kind of briefing.

itens.t: Every number in the article, in the order it appears
itens.porque: A CEO needs the information that changes a decision. The rest can wait until someone asks.

itens.t: What happened, in one or two sentences
itens.porque: Without the story, the details have nothing to hang on. One or two sentences is usually enough.

itens.t: Who says each important piece of information
itens.porque: A figure from the company and a figure from a union or a consultant are not worth the same, and the CEO cannot see the article.

itens.t: The article read out word for word
itens.porque: Reading it out takes longer than the CEO has, and it leaves the choosing to them.

itens.t: Your opinion, before any of the facts
itens.porque: Your reading is useful at the end, marked as yours. Said first, it sounds like one of the facts.

itens.t: Which parts have already happened, and which are only expected or possible
itens.porque: A forecast repeated as a fact can end up in someone else's decision as a fact.

sec1.rationale: The story, who says each important part, and how sure it is. The rest the CEO can ask for.

sec3.titulo: Read it once, for the story
abertura: A short news item about a different sector. Read it once, without stopping on single words.

doc.titulo: A dry winter, a late harvest
doc.texto:
A coffee cooperative in the south of Minas Gerais says this year’s harvest started two to three weeks late, after an unusually dry winter. The cooperative, which has about 4,000 member farms, says it hired about 1,500 seasonal workers, fewer than last year.

A meteorologist at the national weather service expects El Niño conditions to last into March. An agricultural economist at a university in the state estimates that the region’s production could fall by between 2 and 3 million bags, but she said the figure “depends on the rain in the next two months.”

The cooperative has not said how much it will pay seasonal workers next season.

abertura: Mark the **two** sentences that sum up the article.

itens.t: The cooperative hired more seasonal workers than last year.
itens.porque: The article says it hired about 1,500, fewer than last year.

itens.t: The harvest was late after a dry winter, and production may fall.
itens.porque: The first two paragraphs, together: the late start, and the estimate of what could happen to production.

itens.t: The economist says production will fall by exactly 3 million bags.
itens.porque: She gives a range, between 2 and 3 million bags, and says it depends on the rain.

itens.t: There is a forecast about the weather and an estimate about production, from two different people.
itens.porque: The meteorologist expects El Niño to last into March; the economist estimates the fall in production.

itens.t: The cooperative has published what it will pay next season.
itens.porque: The last sentence says the opposite: it has not said how much it will pay.

sec3.rationale: The story is the late harvest and what it could mean. The forecasts come from people outside the cooperative.

abertura: The same news item. Read it again and say where each piece of information comes from.

itens.t: The harvest started two to three weeks late.
itens.porque: “A coffee cooperative … says this year’s harvest started two to three weeks late.” The verb says carries the source.

itens.t: El Niño conditions will last into March.
itens.porque: The meteorologist at the national weather service expects it. It is a forecast, not something that has happened.

itens.t: Production could fall by between 2 and 3 million bags.
itens.porque: The agricultural economist estimates it. The cooperative gives no production figure.

itens.t: Seasonal workers will get 10% more next season.
itens.porque: No pay figure appears: “The cooperative has not said how much it will pay seasonal workers next season.”

itens.t: About 1,500 seasonal workers were hired this year.
itens.porque: “… says it hired about 1,500 seasonal workers.”

itens.t: The production figure depends on the rain in the next two months.
itens.porque: The same economist: the figure “depends on the rain in the next two months.”

sec4.rationale: Three sources in three short paragraphs, and one figure that nobody in the article gives.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. All five sentences are about the same news item.

itens.t: The harvest started
alts: late of two to three weeks
two to three weeks late
two until three weeks late
itens.porque: The length comes before late, and two numbers in a range are joined with to: two to three weeks late.

itens.t: The cooperative hired
alts: around of 1,500 seasonal workers
1,500 of seasonal workers
about 1,500 seasonal workers
itens.porque: About goes straight before the number, with no of. One thousand five hundred.

itens.t: Production could fall by
alts: between 2 and 3 million bags
between 2 to 3 millions bags
among 2 and 3 million bags
itens.porque: Between takes and. After a number, million has no s: three million bags.

itens.t: The cooperative has not said
alts: how much will it pay seasonal workers
how much it will pay seasonal workers
how much pays it seasonal workers
itens.ok: how much it will pay seasonal workers
itens.porque: Inside a sentence, the question keeps statement order: how much it will pay.

itens.t: A meteorologist expects El Niño conditions
alts: lasting into March
that last into March
to last into March
itens.porque: Expect is followed by to + verb. It marks something that has not happened yet.

abertura: Complete each sentence so that the source, or what is missing, is in the sentence. You can use these sentences in your lesson.
itens: "{According to} the cooperative, the harvest started two to three weeks late."
"That figure {comes from} an economist, not from the cooperative."
"The article {does not say} how much the workers will be paid."
"{My reading is} that the weather is only part of the story."

itens.t: The detour adds nine to twelve days to each trip.
itens.porque: “The detour adds nine to twelve days to each trip, according to two of the largest carriers.”

itens.t: Norvale will hire up to 300 temporary workers before November.
itens.porque: “The company says it will hire up to 300 temporary workers before November.” It is a plan, and the company has not said for how long.

itens.t: At least 60 people have left the largest site since April.
itens.porque: “A union representative at the largest site says at least 60 people have left since April.” Norvale has not confirmed that figure.

itens.t: Between 800 and 1,200 warehouse jobs could move to temporary contracts.
itens.porque: Brightline Advisory “estimates that between 800 and 1,200 warehouse jobs in the state could move to temporary contracts if the detour lasts into next year.”

itens.t: The route will reopen by the end of the year.
itens.porque: “The carriers expect the route to reopen by the end of the year.” It is their expectation, and an analyst says it could be March.

itens.t: Norvale is closing its Campinas site.
itens.porque: The article says only that “Norvale declined to comment on its plans for its Campinas site.” Nobody says it is closing.

ev4.rationale: Two statements from the carriers, one from the company, one from the union, one estimate from a consultancy, and one that sounds like news and is not in the article: the Campinas site.

itens.t: adds nine to twelve days to each trip
itens.porque: “The detour adds nine to twelve days to each trip.” The ships are taking the long way now.

itens.t: will hire up to 300 temporary workers
itens.porque: “The company says it will hire…” Will after says is a plan the company announces, not a hire that has happened.

itens.t: could move to temporary contracts
itens.porque: “… could move to temporary contracts if the detour lasts into next year.” Could and if make it a possibility.

itens.t: moved its largest site to 12-hour shifts
itens.porque: “… says it moved its largest site to 12-hour shifts on arrival days in May.” The change was made in May and the shifts continue.

itens.t: could easily be March
itens.porque: The analyst “said it could easily be March.” It is one person’s view of a possible date.

itens.t: expect the route to reopen
itens.porque: “The carriers expect the route to reopen by the end of the year.” An expectation is about the future.

cl4.rationale: Two of each. A briefing that drops these words turns a possibility into a plan, and a plan into a fact.

abertura: A quick reference to the situation and the language you used.

callout.texto: When a number comes with up to or at least, ask: is this the most, or the least? Up to 300 could be 120. At least 60 could be 90.
